calls.head: Horvat gets company tonight
calls.body: At home, the Kings keep sending Byfield’s line (Moore, Byfield and Perry) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Peter Laviolette has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Islanders’ first line is Holmström, Horvat and Palmieri.

calls.head: Don’t buy Kuemper’s record against the Islanders
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Kuemper has been a wall against the Islanders, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if the Islanders finally get to him.

surprises.head: The Islanders hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: The Islanders usually hit more than most teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 57 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 110 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: Schenn has a goal and two assists as the Islanders beat the Kings
paras: Tony DeAngelo played his 500th NHL game. Brayden Schenn opened the scoring for the Islanders early in the first, but Trevor Moore made it 1-1 for Los Angeles just over three minutes later. Matthew Schaefer restored the Islanders’ lead on the power play just over four minutes later. Victor Eklund made it 3-1 early in the second, his fourth straight game with a goal. Quinton Byfield cut the Islanders’ lead to 3-2 on the power play a little over two minutes later, with Kevin Fiala picking up his 300th NHL assist on the goal. DeAngelo and Corey Perry fought midway through the second. Simon Holmström stretched the lead to 4-2 just 39 seconds into the third, and Bo Horvat added an empty-net goal with less than three minutes left to make it 5-2. Fiala played his first game of the season, after missing the first 16, and picked up an assist. Schenn finished with a goal and two assists.

The score flatters the Islanders: the Kings had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Kings win about six in ten. Ilya Sorokin made 26 saves for the Isles, and Darcy Kuemper stopped 16 of 20 at the other end. The Islanders improved to 8-6-4, fifth in the Metropolitan, while the Kings dropped to 5-10-2, seventh in the Pacific.

items.text: The Islanders won for the first time in five games.
The Kings are on a three-game losing streak.

The Islanders won without Mathew Barzal, Alexander Romanov, Jean-Gabriel Pageau and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Mammoth were missing more at the time.
NHL.com had projected the Islanders with 12 forwards and six defensemen, but they dressed 11 and seven.
